question: Should OpenClaw add a per-target subagent concurrency contract, and should its public shape be `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` with the existing global subagent lane retained as the outer cap?
rationale: Source inspection proves the capability is missing, but the repository’s high bar for configuration additions and the competing target, parent, and named-lane semantics require a deliberate public contract before implementation.

options.title: Add hierarchical target caps
options.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` and enforce it per spawned target beneath the existing global subagent budget for native and ACP runs.

options.title: Use named spawn lanes
options.body: Handle resource isolation through the broader caller-selected lane model tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/10467 instead of adding a target-specific setting.

options.title: Keep one global cap
options.body: Decline another configuration surface and document separate gateways or external model-capacity controls as the operational boundary.

recommendation.title: Add hierarchical target caps
recommendation.body: Add `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` and enforce it per spawned target beneath the existing global subagent budget for native and ACP runs.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history trail connects this contract decision to the central agent-limit and command-lane implementation.
